cards.headline: Too personal for The Wall
cards.snippet: Roger Waters wrote this Pink Floyd song, originally titled "Anzio, 1944", at the same time as The Wall, and it was meant for that album. The other band members rejected it because they found it too personal. It was instead recorded and released as a 7" single on 26 July 1982. Though labelled as taken from The Final Cut, it only joined that album in its 2004 remaster.

cards.headline: Waters unveiled a memorial 70 years to the day
cards.snippet: On 18 February 2014, exactly 70 years after his father Eric was killed at Anzio, Italy, Roger Waters unveiled a memorial to his father and the 8th Battalion near the site of the battle. For years he hadn't known the details of that day. Then Harry Shindler, a 93-year-old Anzio veteran, uncovered the precise time and place of the death. Both men attended the unveiling, and it gave Waters some closure.
cards.context: Veteran Harry Shindler had uncovered the exact time and place of the death.

cards.headline: So perfect it ruins every song after it
cards.snippet: the problem with this song is that it's so perfect that you can't hear any other song after this... they're all spoiled by its perfection
cards.context: Top-liked comment; the author later clarified they just sit in silence afterward.

replies.text: A personal song no doubt.  That's why it hits you in the feels because its about his dad.  My grandfather was there at Salerno and Anzio (36th Texas Infantry).

cards.headline: My grandfather was at Anzio
cards.snippet: My Grandfather was at Anzio.  36th Texas.  One of the best tributes ever.  So many brave boys lost.

cards.snippet: Best Pink Floyd song, and it's an unwanted bastard.

cards.headline: The last line is a gut punch
cards.snippet: Up until the last line, it's framed almost like a song about heroes that would be sung at a memorial.
cards.context: Analysis of how the song turns from reverence to bitterness.

replies.author: @lostielizzie
replies.text: Never thought about it this way. Very haunting way of looking at it, but beautiful for the love he clearly had for his daddy.

cards.headline: Roger Waters plays it live for the first time, with MusiCorps
cards.snippet: Premiered live on 16 October 2015 at DAR Constitution Hall, Washington, DC, at Music Heals, a benefit for wounded veterans with the MusiCorps Band. One listener: "G. E. Smith on slide guitar. Nice!"

cards.headline: It opens Pink Floyd – The Wall
cards.snippet: In the 1982 film, the first verse plays over the film's opening, and the second verse returns after "Another Brick in the Wall, Part 1" as Pink finds his father's belongings.
cards.context: Sets up the story premise of the film.
